html:
A great storm surge on the night of 31 January to 1 February 1953 that flooded the coasts of the Netherlands, England and Belgium. In the Netherlands it drowned some 1,800 people.

A strong storm over the North Sea coincided with a high spring tide, and pushed the water up to levels not seen for centuries. In the southwest of the Netherlands, in Zeeland and the islands of South Holland, the sea broke through dikes in dozens of places in the middle of the night. Many people were asleep, and there was little warning, as radio stations were off the air at night. Whole villages went under.

England's east coast was also hit, and about 300 people died there.

The shock led the Dutch to build the Delta Works, a chain of dams and barriers to shut out the sea. In Britain it led in time to the Thames Barrier, which protects London. Much of the Netherlands lies below sea level, and the disaster showed how exposed it still was.
sum: A great storm surge on the night of 31 January to 1 February 1953 that flooded the coasts of the Netherlands, England and Belgium. In the Netherlands it drowned some 1,800 people.
